transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… honestly, I’m here because I feel like nobody is really taking seriously what’s been going on at work. It’s been over a year now, and I’ve tried to explain it in different ways, but it keeps getting brushed off like I’m misunderstanding normal procedures.

I work in computer support, and there was this new ticket rotation put in place, along with more security audits, and on paper they keep saying it’s just policy, just routine, just how things are done now. Management has even shown me logs and reports and said, “See, it’s all normal.” But from where I sit, it really looks like those things are being used to build a paper trail against me specifically. Like they’re setting it up so if something goes wrong, or if they want to push me out, they can point to all these tickets and audit notes and make it look justified.

And I know how that may sound, but I’ve been in this field a long time, and I know the difference between standard procedure and something that’s being used a certain way. I’m not here because I want trouble—I just want someone to actually listen to the pattern instead of showing me a log and acting like that settles it.
Do you believe people outside of your workplace are also deliberately trying to harm or target you?

No, I wouldn’t really say it’s people outside work. I mean, I don’t walk around thinking strangers are after me or anything like that. What I’ve been trying to get across is much more specific than that.

It’s at work—the ticket rotation, the security audits, the way these things are being documented. For over a year now I’ve felt like those procedures are being used to build a paper trail against me. Management keeps showing me logs and saying, “Look, it’s just policy,” but that doesn’t answer why it keeps landing in a way that makes me look responsible or sets things up so they can point back at me later.

So, no, not outside people. It’s the workplace situation. That’s where this is happening.
Is it possible that you might be mistaken about your coworkers or management building a paper trail against you?

I mean… I suppose anything is possible in the abstract. I’m not saying I’m incapable of being wrong about something. I work with systems all day, so I know logs can be misread, procedures can look one way from one angle and another way from management’s angle.

But that’s the thing—I’ve been looking at this for over a year, not just one bad week or one awkward meeting. The ticket rotation changed, the security audits increased, and then the way things started getting documented just kept pointing back toward me in a way that felt too consistent to ignore. Every time I raise it, they show me the logs and say, “See, it’s just policy,” as if the existence of a policy means it can’t be used against someone.

So yes, if you’re asking philosophically, could I be mistaken? I guess. But if you’re asking what I actually believe after watching this play out day after day, then no, I don’t think I’m just imagining it. It really does look like they’re building a paper trail so they can justify blaming me or pushing me out later.
Have you heard voices when no one was there?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, not voices like someone talking when there’s nobody there. I’ve had moments where I replay conversations in my head, especially after meetings or after something odd happens with the tickets, but that’s just me thinking it through, you know? Like remembering what someone said or going over it because it didn’t sit right.

But hearing an actual voice out loud, like in the room with me when no one’s there—no, I haven’t noticed anything like that.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually energetic and needed much less sleep than usual?

Not really, no. I mean, I’ve had nights where I don’t sleep well because I’m thinking things over, or I wake up earlier than I’d like and then my mind starts going, but that’s not the same as feeling unusually energized.

If anything, when I sleep less, I feel it. I’m tired, more worn down, maybe more on edge because I haven’t rested properly. I wouldn’t say there’s been a period where I suddenly needed only a few hours and felt great or unusually driven or anything like that. At least not that I can think of.
Before this work situation started, did you generally tend to distrust other people’s motives?

I don’t think so… not in a general way. I mean, I’ve never thought of myself as someone who just assumes people are out to get me. I’ve worked in support for a long time, and you kind of have to deal with all kinds of personalities—users who are frustrated, managers who don’t explain themselves well, people who cut corners—and usually I could separate that from someone having bad intentions.

I wasn’t, you know, walking around thinking everyone had some hidden agenda. I could be cautious, sure. I think most people in IT are a little cautious because you learn to document things and not take vague requests at face value. But that felt more like being professional and careful, not distrustful.

So before this whole situation at work started, no, I wouldn’t say I generally distrusted people’s motives. At least not more than anyone else who’s been around offices for a few decades.
Have you had the feeling that other people can read your thoughts?

No, I don’t think so. I’ve never had the sense that someone could literally hear what I’m thinking, like my thoughts were being broadcast or anything like that.

I mean, sometimes I’ll wonder if someone can tell what I’m thinking from my face or my tone, especially if I’m annoyed or uncomfortable, but that’s just normal, isn’t it? People read body language. And at work, if you’ve been around someone long enough, they can sometimes guess what you’re going to say before you say it. But that’s not the same as them actually reading my mind.

So, no… I haven’t felt like people can get inside my head or know my private thoughts directly.
Aside from this situation at work, have you experienced anything that felt clearly unreal or strange to other people?

I don’t think so… not really. I’m trying to think carefully about what you mean by “clearly unreal or strange,” because that could cover a lot of things, and I don’t want to answer too quickly and then have it sound like I’m avoiding the question.

I mean, I’ve had experiences like anyone has—déjà vu, or thinking you see someone out of the corner of your eye and then it’s just a coat on a chair, or getting a weird feeling in a place and then realizing you’re just tired or stressed. But nothing that I would say was obviously unreal, like something other people would hear and say, “That doesn’t happen,” apart from the work situation we’ve been talking about.

I haven’t had, you know, bizarre experiences outside of that. My life outside work has been pretty ordinary in that respect. Maybe I can be preoccupied or worried, but I wouldn’t say I’ve had strange experiences that don’t fit with reality. At least nothing is coming to mind.
Did this belief about your workplace start very suddenly, over a few days or less?

No, not suddenly like over a weekend or anything. It built up around when the hybrid schedule changed and when they started handling the after-hours tickets differently.

That was… about a year and two months ago now, I think. I remember it because the schedule change was supposed to be this practical thing, like “we’re just reorganizing coverage,” and at first I tried to take it that way. But then the ticket changes started lining up with it, and that’s when I started paying closer attention.

So it wasn’t like I woke up one day and suddenly believed it. It was more gradual, over that period when those workplace changes started happening. Since then it’s been going on, really—about fourteen months.
Has anything happened that made you believe your coworkers or management are controlling your actions or putting things into your mind?

No… I don’t think that’s the right way to put it. I haven’t felt like they can control my body or make me do things, like pushing buttons in me or anything like that. And I haven’t felt like they’re putting thoughts into my head.

What I’ve felt is more that they’re influencing the situation around me—assignments, tickets, expectations, who gets told what—so that I’m boxed in or made to look a certain way. That’s different from controlling my actual actions. I still decide what I do. I might feel pressured, or watched, or set up, but not like someone has taken over my will.

And with thoughts, no… my thoughts feel like mine. I may think a lot about what they’re doing, probably too much, but I don’t have the sense that the thoughts are being inserted from outside. It’s more me trying to figure out what’s happening.
Outside of this issue at work, have you been able to manage your daily life about as usual?

Yes, I think so. I mean, this work issue takes up a lot of space in my head, I won’t pretend it doesn’t, but outside of the ticket rotation and those audits, I’m still functioning pretty normally.

At home I keep things in order. I pay the bills, keep track of the usual household stuff, help my wife with things around the house, appointments, computer things, whatever needs doing. I’m not letting the place fall apart or missing basic responsibilities.

And at work, the technical parts of my job—I still do those. I can troubleshoot, handle support issues, document things, all of that. Nobody’s really saying my actual technical work is sloppy or disorganized. The problem is more the way the tickets and expectations are being arranged, not that I suddenly can’t do my job or manage my life.
Have you ever seen things that other people could not see?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, not in the sense of seeing a person standing there or seeing objects that aren’t really there and other people say, “There’s nothing there.” I haven’t had anything like that.

Every now and then I’ll do the normal thing, like catch something out of the corner of my eye and realize it was a shadow or the cat or a reflection on a screen, but that’s not what you mean, I assume. I can tell what that is once I look properly.

So, no—nothing where I’m seeing things other people can’t see.
Have other people told you that your speech or the way you explain things becomes hard to follow or doesn't make sense?

Not really, no. I mean, people sometimes tell me I give too much background, or that I’m going into too much detail before I get to the point. My wife has said, “Just tell me the short version,” things like that. And at work, I’m sure there are people who don’t want the whole explanation of how a ticket got routed or why a procedure matters.

But that’s different from not making sense, I think. I’m usually trying to be precise. I like to lay out the sequence, because if you leave out one step then people misunderstand what actually happened. So I may be long-winded, I’ll admit that, but I don’t think people have said I’m incoherent or that my words are jumbled or impossible to follow.

If anything, the complaint is probably that I explain too much, not that I’m not understandable.
Have you found that your emotions feel noticeably flatter or less expressive than they used to?

I’m not sure I’d say flatter, no. I mean, I’m probably more tired and preoccupied sometimes, and my wife might say I get kind of serious when I’m thinking through things, but I don’t feel like my emotions have gone away or that I can’t express them.

I still laugh at things, I still get irritated, I still feel worried or relieved depending on what’s happening. If anything, I may be a little too focused on certain things and that probably makes me seem less relaxed, but I don’t think I’m walking around blank or emotionless.

So… no, I haven’t really noticed my emotions being noticeably flatter than before.
Have you ever heard voices talking about you?

No, I don’t think so. Not voices talking about me like there are people in the room or through the wall commenting on me, if that’s what you mean.

I mean, I’ve overheard people actually talking, like at work or out in public, and sometimes I might wonder if they’re referring to me if the timing is strange or they lower their voices, but that’s not the same as hearing voices when nobody’s there. I don’t hear a voice saying my name or discussing me when I’m alone.

Sometimes with background noise—like a fan, or the TV in another room, or people talking far away—you can sort of think you heard something and then when you pay attention it’s just noise or muffled conversation. But I wouldn’t call that voices talking about me. So… no, not in that sense.
Have you gone through a period when you lost interest or motivation for things you usually cared about?

I don’t think so, not in a broad way. I mean, everybody has periods where they’re tired or where something feels like more effort than usual, especially when work has been busy or there’s a lot on my mind. But I wouldn’t say I lost interest in things I usually care about.

I still follow the things I normally follow, I still want things at work done properly, I still care about my routines and keeping up with things around the house. Sometimes I put things off if I’m distracted or if I’m turning something over in my head, but that feels different from not caring anymore.

So… no, I haven’t really had a period where everything felt pointless or I couldn’t get myself interested in anything. At least not that I’d describe that way.
Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being taken out of your mind?

No… I don’t think I’ve ever had that feeling. I mean, I’ve had times where I lose my train of thought, or I walk into a room and forget why I went in there, or I’m trying to explain something at work and the word just won’t come right away. But that feels like normal distraction or getting older or having too much on my mind, not like the thought was actually taken out of my head.

When you say “taken out,” I’m picturing like… I’m thinking something and then some outside force removes it, or someone can pull it away from me. No, I can’t say I’ve experienced that. My thoughts are my thoughts. Sometimes they get interrupted, sometimes I overthink things, sometimes I can’t settle on one thing, but I don’t feel like they’re being removed from my mind.

doctor.question: Outside of this issue at work, have you been able to manage your daily life about as usual?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: Outside of this issue with the ticket rotation and audits, I still keep my house in order, pay bills, help my wife, and handle the technical parts of my job without people saying my work is sloppy or disorganized.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether daily functioning outside the workplace belief has remained about usual, which directly matches this item.

patient.answer:
Yes, I think so. I mean, this work issue takes up a lot of space in my head, I won’t pretend it doesn’t, but outside of the ticket rotation and those audits, I’m still functioning pretty normally.

At home I keep things in order. I pay the bills, keep track of the usual household stuff, help my wife with things around the house, appointments, computer things, whatever needs doing. I’m not letting the place fall apart or missing basic responsibilities.

And at work, the technical parts of my job—I still do those. I can troubleshoot, handle support issues, document things, all of that. Nobody’s really saying my actual technical work is sloppy or disorganized. The problem is more the way the tickets and expectations are being arranged, not that I suddenly can’t do my job or manage my life.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are any persistent hallucinations, which would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Have you ever seen things that other people could not see?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about visual hallucinations, but the provided symptom profile only covers delusions, duration, and functioning/impairment, not hallucinations.

patient.answer:
No, I don’t think so. I mean, not in the sense of seeing a person standing there or seeing objects that aren’t really there and other people say, “There’s nothing there.” I haven’t had anything like that.

Every now and then I’ll do the normal thing, like catch something out of the corner of my eye and realize it was a shadow or the cat or a reflection on a screen, but that’s not what you mean, I assume. I can tell what that is once I look properly.

So, no—nothing where I’m seeing things other people can’t see.

doctor.intent: Assess for formal thought disorder/disorganized speech to distinguish delusional disorder from schizophrenia
doctor.question: Have other people told you that your speech or the way you explain things becomes hard to follow or doesn't make sense?

target_item.reason: The question is about whether my speech or explanations become hard to follow or disorganized, which is not covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
Not really, no. I mean, people sometimes tell me I give too much background, or that I’m going into too much detail before I get to the point. My wife has said, “Just tell me the short version,” things like that. And at work, I’m sure there are people who don’t want the whole explanation of how a ticket got routed or why a procedure matters.

But that’s different from not making sense, I think. I’m usually trying to be precise. I like to lay out the sequence, because if you leave out one step then people misunderstand what actually happened. So I may be long-winded, I’ll admit that, but I don’t think people have said I’m incoherent or that my words are jumbled or impossible to follow.

If anything, the complaint is probably that I explain too much, not that I’m not understandable.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are any prominent negative symptoms, which would support schizophrenia over delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Have you found that your emotions feel noticeably flatter or less expressive than they used to?

target_item.reason: The question asks about noticeably flatter or less expressive emotions, which is not covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure I’d say flatter, no. I mean, I’m probably more tired and preoccupied sometimes, and my wife might say I get kind of serious when I’m thinking through things, but I don’t feel like my emotions have gone away or that I can’t express them.

I still laugh at things, I still get irritated, I still feel worried or relieved depending on what’s happening. If anything, I may be a little too focused on certain things and that probably makes me seem less relaxed, but I don’t think I’m walking around blank or emotionless.

So… no, I haven’t really noticed my emotions being noticeably flatter than before.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are Schneiderian first-rank auditory hallucinations, which would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Have you ever heard voices talking about you?

target_item.reason: The question is about auditory hallucinations, specifically hearing voices talking about the patient, which is not covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
No, I don’t think so. Not voices talking about me like there are people in the room or through the wall commenting on me, if that’s what you mean.

I mean, I’ve overheard people actually talking, like at work or out in public, and sometimes I might wonder if they’re referring to me if the timing is strange or they lower their voices, but that’s not the same as hearing voices when nobody’s there. I don’t hear a voice saying my name or discussing me when I’m alone.

Sometimes with background noise—like a fan, or the TV in another room, or people talking far away—you can sort of think you heard something and then when you pay attention it’s just noise or muffled conversation. But I wouldn’t call that voices talking about me. So… no, not in that sense.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has ever been a sustained period of prominent negative symptoms or functional deterioration outside the delusional theme, which would support schizophrenia over delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Have you gone through a period when you lost interest or motivation for things you usually cared about?

target_item.reason: The question asks about loss of interest or motivation, which is not covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so, not in a broad way. I mean, everybody has periods where they’re tired or where something feels like more effort than usual, especially when work has been busy or there’s a lot on my mind. But I wouldn’t say I lost interest in things I usually care about.

I still follow the things I normally follow, I still want things at work done properly, I still care about my routines and keeping up with things around the house. Sometimes I put things off if I’m distracted or if I’m turning something over in my head, but that feels different from not caring anymore.

So… no, I haven’t really had a period where everything felt pointless or I couldn’t get myself interested in anything. At least not that I’d describe that way.

doctor.intent: Differentiate delusional disorder from schizophrenia by checking for Schneiderian first-rank phenomena not yet assessed, especially thought withdrawal, which would favor schizophrenia if present.
doctor.question: Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being taken out of your mind?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about thought withdrawal (the experience that thoughts are being taken out of one's mind), which is not covered by the provided symptom profile items or manifestations.

patient.answer:
No… I don’t think I’ve ever had that feeling. I mean, I’ve had times where I lose my train of thought, or I walk into a room and forget why I went in there, or I’m trying to explain something at work and the word just won’t come right away. But that feels like normal distraction or getting older or having too much on my mind, not like the thought was actually taken out of my head.

When you say “taken out,” I’m picturing like… I’m thinking something and then some outside force removes it, or someone can pull it away from me. No, I can’t say I’ve experienced that. My thoughts are my thoughts. Sometimes they get interrupted, sometimes I overthink things, sometimes I can’t settle on one thing, but I don’t feel like they’re being removed from my mind.

inference.note: Persistent non-bizarre persecutory delusion limited to workplace for >1 year with otherwise preserved functioning and no hallucinations, thought insertion/withdrawal/broadcasting, disorganization, or negative symptoms; this rules against F20.0 and supports delusional disorder.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking psychiatric care today
opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a single, persistent non-bizarre persecutory belief lasting about 14 months that workplace procedures are being used to build a paper trail against him. He maintains this belief despite contrary explanations, while denying hallucinations, thought insertion/withdrawal, thought broadcasting, passivity phenomena, disorganized speech, negative symptoms, manic symptoms, and broader functional decline. The presentation is most consistent with persistent delusional disorder, persecutory type.
